title: Why psychological safety matters in a changing workplace, with Dennis Stolle, PhD

sentences.en: Four years after the COVID-19 pandemic upended work life in the U.S., companies and workers are still adjusting to the new normal.
sentences.zh: 在美国新冠疫情彻底改变职场生活的四年后，企业和员工仍在适应这种“新常态”。

sentences.en: In June, APA's annual Work in America survey found that many workers are doing well and feeling satisfied with key aspects of their jobs, but some younger workers are struggling.
sentences.zh: 今年6月，美国心理学会（APA）的年度“美国职场调查”显示，许多员工工作状态良好，对工作的关键方面感到满意，但一些年轻员工却感到挣扎。

sentences.en: They're more likely than older workers to feel stressed, lonely, and undervalued at work.
sentences.zh: 与年长员工相比，他们更容易在工作中感到压力、孤独和价值被低估。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk about that, as well as other key findings from the survey, which examined some of the biggest issues facing employees and employers today.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将讨论这一问题，以及该调查的其他关键发现，这些发现审视了当今员工和雇主所面临的一些重大议题。

sentences.en: Why are younger workers struggling?
sentences.zh: 为什么年轻员工会感到挣扎？

sentences.en: How do employees feel about remote work, hybrid work, and four-day work weeks?
sentences.zh: 员工对远程办公、混合办公和四天工作制有何看法？

sentences.en: How is artificial intelligence affecting the workplace?
sentences.zh: 人工智能对职场有何影响？

sentences.en: Are workers using it, and are employers prepared to handle the changes it may bring?
sentences.zh: 员工们在使用它吗？雇主们是否准备好应对它可能带来的变革？

sentences.en: Overall, how are workers feeling about their jobs?
sentences.zh: 总体而言，员工对自己的工作感觉如何？

sentences.en: And what can employers do to create supportive workplaces where employees can thrive?
sentences.zh: 雇主又能做些什么来创造支持性的工作环境，让员工能够茁壮成长？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Dennis Stolle, Senior Director of APA's Office of Applied Psychology, which focuses on applying psychological science to help solve real-world probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是丹尼斯·斯托尔（Dennis Stolle）博士，他是美国心理学会应用心理学办公室的高级主任，该办公室专注于应用心理科学来帮助解决现实世界的问题。

sentences.en: It looks at areas including the workplace, human technology interaction, and leadership, to name just a few areas.
sentences.zh: 其研究领域包括职场、人机交互和领导力等，这仅是其中几个方面。

sentences.en: Dr. Stolle holds a Ph.D.
sentences.zh: 斯托尔博士拥有社会与人格心理学博士学位，

sentences.en: in social and personality psychology, as well as a law degree.
sentences.zh: 同时也拥有法律学位。

sentences.en: He's discussed workplace issues with media outlets, including The Washington Post, The New York Times, and CNN.com,
sentences.zh: 他曾与《华盛顿邮报》、《纽约时报》和CNN.com等媒体讨论过职场问题，

sentences.en: and has published widely in both academic journals and popular media.
sentences.zh: 并在学术期刊和大众媒体上发表过大量文章。

sentences.en: Dr. Stolle, or may I call you Dennis, my colleague, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 斯托尔博士，或者我可以叫你丹尼斯，我的同事，感谢你今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: Well, thank you very much for having me.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: So I mentioned in the introduction that there was an overall trend in this year's Work in America survey that found younger employees are struggling more than older employees,
sentences.zh: 我在开场白中提到，今年“美国职场调查”的一个总体趋势是，年轻员工比年长员工面临更多的挣扎，

sentences.en: feeling undervalued and underappreciated at work.
sentences.zh: 在工作中感到价值被低估和不受重视。

sentences.en: Can you tell us more about that?
sentences.zh: 你能详细谈谈这一点吗？

sentences.en: What did the survey find, and why do you think we're seeing this trend?
sentences.zh: 调查发现了什么？你认为我们为什么会看到这种趋势？

sentences.en: So one of the topics that we asked about in the survey was whether workers felt that their co-workers
sentences.zh: 我们在调查中询问的一个话题是，员工是否觉得他们的同事

sentences.en: who were outside their age group appreciated and saw the value in the ideas that they were presenting at work.
sentences.zh: ——那些不在他们年龄段的同事——是否认可并看到了他们在工作中提出的想法的价值。

sentences.en: And what we found was that almost half of the workers who were aged 18 to 25 said no,
sentences.zh: 结果发现，几乎一半18至25岁的员工回答“没有”，

sentences.en: meaning that they were saying the co-workers outside their age group do not see the value in their ideas.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们认为其他年龄段的同事看不到他们想法的价值。

sentences.en: Now, where it gets interesting is when you compare that number to workers who are aged 65 and older,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当你将这个数字与65岁及以上的员工进行比较时，

sentences.en: among that age group, only 16% said that co-workers outside their age group don't see the value in their ideas.
sentences.zh: 在该年龄段中，只有16%的人表示其他年龄段的同事看不到他们想法的价值。

sentences.en: So we see a big difference at the two ends of the working adult age spectrum.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们在职场成年人年龄谱系的两端看到了巨大的差异。

sentences.en: Now, the survey also found that younger workers are less comfortable than older workers working outside their own age group.
sentences.zh: 此外，调查还发现，年轻员工在与不同年龄段的人共事时，比年长员工感到更不自在。

sentences.en: As you said, why do you think that might be?
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，你认为原因可能是什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有趣。

sentences.en: I have a lot of opinions about that.
sentences.zh: 我对此有很多看法。

sentences.en: One of the things about a survey like this one is that the data tells us if something is happening.
sentences.zh: 像这类调查的一个特点是，数据能告诉我们某件事是否正在发生。

sentences.en: It tells us how often it's happening, and it can even tell us whether two things are happening together so frequently that it's unlikely to just be a coincidence.
sentences.zh: 它能告诉我们这件事发生的频率，甚至能告诉我们两件事是否经常同时发生，以至于不可能是巧合。

sentences.en: But it doesn't ultimately tell us why something is happening.
sentences.zh: 但它最终无法告诉我们这件事为什么会发生。

sentences.en: For that, we have to kind of go beyond the data and look at the teachings of psychology as a science and the literature as a whole.
sentences.zh: 为了弄清原因，我们必须超越数据，审视心理学作为一门科学的理论以及整体文献。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I think really may be at work here is the concept of psychological safety.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里真正起作用的一个概念是“心理安全感”。

sentences.en: Psychological safety is a term of art that gets used within psychological science,
sentences.zh: 心理安全感是心理科学中的一个专业术语，

sentences.en: and it refers to the feeling that people have at work that they can truly express themselves and share their ideas and opinions without any negative consequences.
sentences.zh: 它指的是人们在工作中感到可以真实地表达自我，分享自己的想法和观点，而不会产生任何负面后果的感觉。

sentences.en: And when I say negative consequences,
sentences.zh: 当我提到负面后果时，

sentences.en: I'm talking about things like maybe being laughed at for their idea or maybe being belittled for an idea or just ignored for the idea that they're sharing.
sentences.zh: 我指的是诸如因想法被嘲笑、被贬低，或者仅仅是被忽视等情况。

sentences.en: When people have psychological safety at work, they're able to really express themselves.
sentences.zh: 当人们在工作中拥有心理安全感时，他们能够真正地表达自己。

sentences.en: My sense is that among young workers, they may still be developing that sense of psychological safety.
sentences.zh: 我的感觉是，年轻员工可能还在培养这种心理安全感。

sentences.en: And so when they look around, they may be feeling more comfortable working with other people who are in their own age group because that's where they feel safe.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们环顾四周时，可能会觉得与同龄人共事更自在，因为那是他们感到安全的地方。

sentences.en: And they haven't yet begun to expand their horizons of psychological safety to the entire workforce.
sentences.zh: 他们还没有开始将心理安全感的范围扩展到整个职场。

sentences.en: What can employers do to help these younger workers get that sense of psychological safety?
sentences.zh: 雇主能做些什么来帮助这些年轻员工获得那种心理安全感？

sentences.en: I think that there are, I can name at least five things that a manager could do that are simple and that you could start tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我认为至少有五件事是经理可以做的，它们很简单，而且明天就可以开始。

sentences.en: One is giving constructive feedback, including for a job well done.
sentences.zh: 第一是给予建设性的反馈，包括对出色工作的肯定。

sentences.en: A lot of times I think when we think about constructive feedback, we go right to, well, this is when I have to kind of coach somebody who's made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我认为当我们想到建设性反馈时，会直接想到：好吧，这是我必须指导那些犯了错的人的时候。

sentences.en: And I'm going to have to, you know, not offend them, but teach them how to do it right.
sentences.zh: 我得，你知道，不能冒犯他们，但要教他们如何做对。

sentences.en: I think it's so important to go beyond that.
sentences.zh: 我认为超越这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: When somebody does a good job, even on something very small, to bring that up and celebrate it, especially with somebody who's new to the workforce.
sentences.zh: 当某人做得好时，即使是很小的事情，也要提出来并加以庆祝，特别是对于刚进入职场的人。

sentences.en: Those little reinforcements begin to give people the sense that, hey, I can make a contribution here and I'm important.
sentences.zh: 那些小小的鼓励开始让人们觉得，嘿，我可以在这里做出贡献，我很重要。

sentences.en: And then another thing is to really celebrate teamwork and celebrate collaboration,
sentences.zh: 另一件事是真正地庆祝团队合作和协作，

sentences.en: especially when the teamwork and collaboration spans across the levels of age and experience in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 特别是当这种团队合作和协作跨越了职场中年龄和经验的层级时。

sentences.en: Another thing is emphasizing skills over corporate hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 还有一点是强调技能胜过企业层级。

sentences.en: So, if there's a young worker who maybe has a job title that is lower down, so to speak, on the organizational chart,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有一个年轻员工，他的职位在组织结构图上可能比较低，

sentences.en: that doesn't necessarily mean that they don't have a certain skill.
sentences.zh: 这并不一定意味着他没有某种技能。

sentences.en: And really celebrating those skills over the corporate hierarchy is another way to just begin to make people feel safe about making their contributions in the workplace.
sentences.zh: 真正地庆祝这些技能而不是企业层级，是让人们开始感到在职场中贡献自己的想法是安全的另一种方式。

sentences.en: Is it a question of mentorship?
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于导师制的问题吗？

sentences.en: Do we find that a lot of workplaces don't value the whole idea of helping the more senior employers to really, really help the younger employers in that way?
sentences.zh: 我们是否发现许多职场并不重视帮助资深员工真正地、切实地帮助年轻员工这一理念？

sentences.en: I believe that it is an issue of mentorship, but it goes beyond just mentorship.
sentences.zh: 我相信这是一个导师制的问题，但它不仅仅是导师制。

sentences.en: So, the mentorship is critically important.
sentences.zh: 导师制固然至关重要。

sentences.en: I think that the one-on-one meetings with managers can be critically important.
sentences.zh: 我认为经理与员工的一对一会议也至关重要。

sentences.en: The relationship between a direct report and a supervisor or manager can be critically important in determining the overall experience that a person has in the workplace,
sentences.zh: 直接下属与主管或经理之间的关系，对于决定一个人在职场中的整体体验至关重要，

sentences.en: which is yet another thing that our data showed in the 2024 survey over and over again, just how important that direct report manager relationship is.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们在2024年调查中反复看到的数据，即这种直接汇报关系是多么重要。

sentences.en: But again, I think it goes beyond just that mentorship to a broader organizational culture.
sentences.zh: 但同样，我认为这不仅仅是导师制，还涉及更广泛的组织文化。

sentences.en: There are some organizations, some workplaces that really foster a culture of everybody matters and everybody's ideas are important.
sentences.zh: 有些组织、有些职场确实培养了一种“每个人都很重要，每个人的想法都很重要”的文化。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean that we're going to do everything that everybody suggests, right?
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着我们会采纳每个人提出的所有建议，对吧？

sentences.en: But we'll consider it and we'll celebrate the fact that you're offering ideas, even if they're ideas that we're going to ultimately reject.
sentences.zh: 但我们会考虑它，并会庆祝你提出想法这一事实，即使这些想法最终会被拒绝。

sentences.en: And on the other hand, there are some workplaces that really just don't foster that kind of a culture.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，有些职场确实没有培养这种文化。

sentences.en: They are hierarchical and chain of command and people are fearful that if they step out of their small zone, that there might be a negative consequence.
sentences.zh: 它们等级森严，讲究指挥链，人们担心如果越出自己的小圈子，可能会产生负面后果。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about some of the good news that APA found this year.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们谈谈美国心理学会今年发现的一些好消息。

sentences.en: Many workers are feeling pretty satisfied with key aspects of their jobs.
sentences.zh: 许多员工对工作的关键方面感到相当满意。

sentences.en: What were some of the areas where employees said they were feeling good about their work?
sentences.zh: 员工们表示对工作感到满意的领域有哪些？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: We saw a lot of positive sentiments and we saw them across a range of aspects of the workplace,
sentences.zh: 我们看到了许多积极的情绪，而且它们涵盖了职场的各个方面，

sentences.en: including things that I think are just deeply important and some things that are more superficial.
sentences.zh: 包括我认为非常重要的事物，以及一些比较表面的事物。

sentences.en: When I say superficial, I'm talking about things like people generally reported that they were happy with their work schedule.
sentences.zh: 当我提到表面时，我指的是人们普遍报告说他们对工作时间表感到满意。

sentences.en: Not that that's not important, but it's superficial compared to, for example, being proud of the work that you do or feeling that you're contributing to society.
sentences.zh: 并不是说这不重要，但与例如为你所做的工作感到自豪或感到你正在为社会做出贡献相比，它是表面的。

sentences.en: And that's where I really was happy about some of the numbers that we were seeing.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我对我们看到的一些数据感到高兴的地方。

sentences.en: We were seeing 93% reporting that they're proud of the work that they do.
sentences.zh: 我们看到93%的人报告说他们为自己所做的工作感到自豪。

sentences.en: 86% reporting that they feel that the work they do has a positive impact on society.
sentences.zh: 86%的人报告说他们觉得自己的工作对社会产生了积极影响。

sentences.en: 81% who would recommend their place of employment as a good place to work.
sentences.zh: 81%的人会推荐他们工作的地方作为一个好的工作场所。

sentences.en: Those are the kind of numbers that really go to the core of our being.
sentences.zh: 这些数字真正触及了我们存在的核心。

sentences.en: You know, why do you get up every day?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你每天为什么要起床？

sentences.en: Because you want to go do work that you're proud of and it has a positive contribution.
sentences.zh: 因为你想去做你引以为豪的工作，并且它有积极的贡献。

sentences.en: And so when I see those kinds of numbers, I feel very good about the state of the situation.
sentences.zh: 所以当我看到这些数字时，我对现状感觉非常好。

sentences.en: One of the biggest shifts in the past four years has been toward remote and hybrid work.
sentences.zh: 过去四年中最大的转变之一是向远程和混合办公的转变。

sentences.en: What percentage of workers are working remote, in-person, and hybrid these days?
sentences.zh: 如今有多少比例的员工在进行远程、线下和混合办公？

sentences.en: And how does work location affect people's job satisfaction?
sentences.zh: 工作地点如何影响人们的工作满意度？

sentences.en: Okay, so these were some really interesting numbers because what we saw is that 59% of the respondents reported that they were working in-person.
sentences.zh: 好的，这些数字非常有趣，因为我们看到59%的受访者报告说他们是在线下办公。

sentences.en: We had 24% reporting that they were working hybrid, some mix of in-person and remote, and 17% reporting that they were working remote.
sentences.zh: 24%的人报告说他们是混合办公，即线下和远程的某种组合，17%的人报告说他们是远程办公。

sentences.en: Now, those numbers are mildly interesting on their own.
sentences.zh: 这些数字本身就很有趣。

sentences.en: But where it gets really interesting is then we ask the next question of where would you most want to be working?
sentences.zh: 但真正有趣的是，当我们问下一个问题：你最想在哪里工作时？

sentences.en: And then we see the numbers break down quite a bit differently.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的数字分布就大不相同了。

sentences.en: Almost an even split of a third, a third, and a third.
sentences.zh: 几乎是三分之一、三分之一、三分之一的均匀分配。

sentences.en: Now, it's not quite that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也不完全是这样。

sentences.en: It was 38% in person, 34% would prefer hybrid, and 28% would prefer remote.
sentences.zh: 38%的人希望线下办公，34%的人更喜欢混合办公，28%的人更喜欢远程办公。

sentences.en: But those numbers are so close to one another that it's almost equal thirds.
sentences.zh: 但这些数字彼此非常接近，几乎是相等的三分之一。

sentences.en: That's fascinating to me because sometimes I hear people just in casual conversation talk about, well, what's the best way to work?
sentences.zh: 这让我感到着迷，因为有时我听到人们在闲聊时谈论，最好的工作方式是什么？

sentences.en: As if there's one correct answer to that.
sentences.zh: 好像对此有一个正确的答案一样。

sentences.en: The reality is that different people have different opinions, different personalities, different positions in their life at a given point in time.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，不同的人有不同的意见、不同的性格、在人生不同阶段有不同的处境。

sentences.en: They might prefer remote work.
sentences.zh: 他们可能更喜欢远程办公。

sentences.en: Somebody else might prefer in-person work.
sentences.zh: 另一个人可能更喜欢线下办公。

sentences.en: That may switch 10 years down the road.
sentences.zh: 十年后情况可能会发生变化。

sentences.en: And then what's a bit troubling is when you think about the difference between equal thirds versus where people are actually working.
sentences.zh: 有点令人不安的是，当你考虑到“相等的三分之一”与人们实际工作地点之间的差异时。

sentences.en: We ran the statistics and found that 33% of people are not currently working in their desired location, either in-person, remote, or hybrid.
sentences.zh: 我们统计后发现，33%的人目前的工作地点并非他们所期望的，无论是线下、远程还是混合办公。

sentences.en: What about four-day work weeks?
sentences.zh: 那四天工作制呢？

sentences.en: Are many employers offering them now?
sentences.zh: 现在有很多雇主提供这种制度吗？

sentences.en: Did four-day work week increase employees' happiness at work?
sentences.zh: 四天工作制是否提高了员工的工作幸福感？

sentences.en: Do we know?
sentences.zh: 我们知道吗？

sentences.en: I don't know that we could say that a lot of employers are offering four-day work weeks, but there is certainly a meaningful percentage who are.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我们能否说有很多雇主提供四天工作制，但确实有相当一部分雇主在这样做。

sentences.en: And that number is increasing.
sentences.zh: 而且这个数字正在增加。

sentences.en: So just to give you a sense of the trend, we asked the question in 2022 in our survey of whether or not your employer is offering four-day work weeks.
sentences.zh: 为了让你了解这个趋势，我们在2022年的调查中询问了你的雇主是否提供四天工作制的问题。

sentences.en: And we had 14% of the respondents say yes.
sentences.zh: 当时有14%的受访者回答“是”。

sentences.en: In 23, that number went up to 17%.
sentences.zh: 2023年，这个数字上升到了17%。

sentences.en: In 24, that number went up to 22%.
sentences.zh: 2024年，这个数字上升到了22%。

sentences.en: So now we're approaching a quarter of the workforce who's reporting that their employer is offering a four-day work week.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们接近四分之一的劳动力报告说他们的雇主提供四天工作制。

sentences.en: Now, it's still early to be able to know the complexities of how a four-day work week would affect people's happiness and how it would affect productivity.
sentences.zh: 现在要了解四天工作制如何影响人们的幸福感以及如何影响生产力的复杂性还为时过早。

sentences.en: It's going to take a little while for that idea to expand so that we can fully study it.
sentences.zh: 这个概念还需要一段时间才能普及，以便我们能够充分研究它。

sentences.en: And what we can study right now is what people think it will result in.
sentences.zh: 我们现在能研究的是人们认为它会带来什么结果。

sentences.en: And there, we see that 81% of workers who are polled say they believe they could be just as effective at their job if they only worked four days a week.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们看到81%的受访员工表示，他们相信如果每周只工作四天，他们同样能高效完成工作。

sentences.en: 79% say they'd be happier if they were working only four days a week.
sentences.zh: 79%的人表示，如果每周只工作四天，他们会更快乐。

sentences.en: And here's what really struck me is 67% of our respondents reported a belief that it is going to become the norm within their lifetime that Americans will work four days a week.
sentences.zh: 真正让我震惊的是，67%的受访者认为，在他们有生之年，美国人每周工作四天将成为常态。

sentences.en: Now, we didn't really dig too deeply into that.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有深入挖掘这一点。

sentences.en: So a four-day work week, you may still be working, say, about 40 hours a week, but it'll be spread over four days instead of over five days, right?
sentences.zh: 所以四天工作制，你可能仍然每周工作大约40小时，但它会分散在四天而不是五天里，对吧？

sentences.en: That's potentially where we're going.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我们前进的方向。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We're not talking about necessarily working fewer hours or switching to a part-time model.
sentences.zh: 我们不一定是指减少工作时间或转向兼职模式。

sentences.en: And in fact, that's a really important distinction that I'm glad you brought up because there are many people who work four days a week right now,
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是一个非常重要的区别，我很高兴你提到了这一点，因为现在有很多人每周工作四天，

sentences.en: and they work just shy of what the law considers to be a full-time job, which then cuts them out of some of the benefits that full-time employees would receive.
sentences.zh: 他们的工作时间刚好低于法律规定的全职工作时间，这使他们无法享受全职员工应得的一些福利。

sentences.en: That's not what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的不是这种情况。

sentences.en: The folks who are in that situation are not necessarily happy about that situation.
sentences.zh: 处于那种情况的人并不一定对现状感到满意。

sentences.en: We're talking about people who are considered full-time employees, are getting all the same benefits as a full-time employee,
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是那些被视为全职员工，享受与全职员工相同的所有福利，

sentences.en: but are putting their work into four days instead of five days.
sentences.zh: 但将工作时间压缩在四天而不是五天的人。

sentences.en: The survey also asked whether employees are using artificial intelligence on the job.
sentences.zh: 调查还询问了员工是否在工作中使用了人工智能。

sentences.en: What did we find?
sentences.zh: 我们发现了什么？

sentences.en: Are people using things like ChatGPT and other AI tools, and are employers prepared to deal with this?
sentences.zh: 人们是否在使用ChatGPT和其他AI工具？雇主们准备好应对了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, this is a tricky thing to study because AI is, in some ways, everywhere.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难研究的问题，因为在某种程度上，人工智能无处不在。

sentences.en: And it's been around for longer than sometimes we may think of it having been around.
sentences.zh: 而且它存在的时间比我们有时意识到的要长。

sentences.en: You know, ChatGPT made everyone aware of AI, but it's been around for a long time before that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，ChatGPT让每个人都意识到了人工智能，但在此之前它已经存在很长时间了。

sentences.en: So, there are a lot of workers who use AI, perhaps unknowingly, while they're at work.
sentences.zh: 所以，有很多员工在工作中可能在不知不觉中使用了人工智能。

sentences.en: So, we didn't want to study that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们不想研究那个。

sentences.en: What we really wanted to do in the survey was get at people who are intentionally using artificial intelligence
sentences.zh: 我们在调查中真正想做的是针对那些有意使用人工智能的人，

sentences.en: specifically for the purpose of helping themselves with their work as part of their employment.
sentences.zh: 即专门为了帮助他们完成工作而将其作为就业一部分的人。

sentences.en: And when we asked that question, we found that there were about a little over a third who reported doing so at least monthly, many of them much more frequently than monthly.
sentences.zh: 当我们提出这个问题时，我们发现有超过三分之一的人表示至少每月会这样做一次，其中许多人的频率远不止每月一次。

sentences.en: And there were also differences across the type of workers.
sentences.zh: 而且不同类型的员工之间也存在差异。

sentences.en: So, we saw that younger workers were using it more.
sentences.zh: 我们观察到，年轻员工使用它的频率更高。

sentences.en: And perhaps that's not surprising, but we also found that younger workers were also more likely than older workers
sentences.zh: 这或许并不令人惊讶，但我们还发现，与年长员工相比，年轻员工更有可能

sentences.en: to report being worried that AI may end up taking some or all of their job duties.
sentences.zh: 表示担心人工智能最终会取代他们部分或全部的工作职责。

sentences.en: So, you've got this situation where they're using it more, but they are also more concerned
sentences.zh: 所以，现在的情况是，他们使用人工智能的频率更高，但同时也更担心

sentences.en: that they may lose some aspects of their job to AI as it progresses and we move into the future.
sentences.zh: 随着人工智能的发展和未来的到来，他们可能会失去部分工作内容。

sentences.en: And my understanding is that the survey also found that a lot of these employees reported that their employers didn't have policies in place.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，调查还发现许多员工反映他们的雇主并没有制定相应的政策。

sentences.en: Is that right, too?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: That is absolutely correct.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So, we asked whether or not their employer had a policy in place on the use of AI to help them with their work.
sentences.zh: 我们询问了雇主是否制定了关于使用人工智能辅助工作的政策。

sentences.en: And only 18% reported that they know that their employer has a policy.
sentences.zh: 只有18%的受访者表示他们知道雇主有相关政策。

sentences.en: 50%, 5-0, 50% said that their employer has no policy.
sentences.zh: 50%的人表示他们的雇主没有任何政策。

sentences.en: And 32% said that they are unsure.
sentences.zh: 还有32%的人表示不确定。

sentences.en: And so, when you look at that data, it paints a picture of a world in which employees are moving faster
sentences.zh: 因此，当你审视这些数据时，它描绘了一个员工在采用人工智能方面

sentences.en: in the adoption of artificial intelligence than perhaps a lot of employer policy manuals are moving.
sentences.zh: 比许多雇主的政策手册更新速度更快的世界。

sentences.en: And so, there's a bit of a mismatch there.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里存在一定程度的脱节。

sentences.en: And that's something that I think is clearly going to need to be addressed by employers.
sentences.zh: 我认为这显然是雇主需要解决的问题。

sentences.en: Now, the survey also looked at the experiences of workers with physical and mental disabilities
sentences.zh: 此外，这项调查还关注了身心障碍员工的经历，

sentences.en: and found that, on average, they are facing more challenges at work and aren't as satisfied with their jobs.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，平均而言，他们在工作中面临更多挑战，对工作的满意度也不如其他人。

sentences.en: What did the data say?
sentences.zh: 数据是怎么说的？

sentences.en: We've talked about a number of things that the data showed that are really positive trends.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了一些数据所显示的非常积极的趋势。

sentences.en: This is one that is very much not a positive trend.
sentences.zh: 但这一个绝非积极的趋势。

sentences.en: There's a robust and troubling trend throughout our data.
sentences.zh: 我们的数据中存在一个显著且令人不安的趋势。

sentences.en: And it shows time and time again that people living with a disability, especially people who are living with a non-physical disability,
sentences.zh: 它一次又一次地表明，残障人士，尤其是患有非身体残障的人，

sentences.en: such as a cognitive, emotional learning disability, are more likely to report things like having a toxic workplace experience.
sentences.zh: 例如认知或情感学习障碍的人，更有可能报告在职场中遭遇有毒的工作环境。

sentences.en: They're more worried that their salary is not keeping pace with inflation.
sentences.zh: 他们更担心自己的薪水跟不上通货膨胀。

sentences.en: They're more worried that AI is going to end up taking away some or all of their job duties.
sentences.zh: 他们更担心人工智能最终会夺走他们部分或全部的工作职责。

sentences.en: In general, there's a trend across so many aspects of the workplace experience where people who are living with a disability
sentences.zh: 总的来说，在职场体验的许多方面都存在一种趋势，即残障人士

sentences.en: are just not doing as well emotionally and psychologically in the workplace as people who are not living with a disability.
sentences.zh: 在职场中的情感和心理状态不如非残障人士那样良好。

sentences.en: And we also dug in and tried to ask questions to find out, you know, what could help.
sentences.zh: 我们也深入挖掘并试图提出问题，找出什么能提供帮助。

sentences.en: And among those who are living with a physical disability, time and time again,
sentences.zh: 在那些有身体残障的人群中，他们反复指出，

sentences.en: what they pointed to was access to resources in the workplace that could help them to get their jobs done.
sentences.zh: 他们需要的是能够帮助他们完成工作的职场资源。

sentences.en: They said that's what they need and that's what could help them have a positive impact on their productivity and just generally be a better worker and a better employee.
sentences.zh: 他们说这是他们所需要的，这能对他们的生产力产生积极影响，并让他们成为更好的员工。

sentences.en: Was there anything in the survey that really surprised you that just jumped out because you weren't expecting it?
sentences.zh: 调查中有什么让你感到惊讶，或者让你印象深刻、出乎意料的事情吗？

sentences.en: One of the things that really surprised me is the extent to which the concept of psychological safety just pervaded the entire survey.
sentences.zh: 让我感到非常惊讶的一点是，“心理安全感”这一概念在整个调查中无处不在。

sentences.en: And again, when I say psychological safety, I'm not talking about, you know, sort of analogous to physical safety.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，当我提到心理安全感时，我指的并不是类似于身体安全的那种概念。

sentences.en: It's not some kind of a hard hat to protect your emotions.
sentences.zh: 它不是保护你情绪的某种安全帽。

sentences.en: Instead, it's this concept that people feel comfortable and safe speaking up in the workplace without fear of negative consequences.
sentences.zh: 相反，它是一个概念，即人们在职场中感到舒适和安全，敢于发言而不用担心负面后果。

sentences.en: And when there's a culture that encourages psychological safety, it has a tremendously beneficial effect on a lot of things that perhaps you might say,
sentences.zh: 当一种文化鼓励心理安全感时，它会对许多事情产生巨大的有益影响，你可能会说，

sentences.en: well, that, you know, that seems reasonable, that makes sense, such as people are more willing to contribute.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这听起来很合理，很有道理，比如人们更愿意做出贡献。

sentences.en: They feel more like they belong in the workplace, this sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们会觉得自己在职场中更有归属感，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But it also seems to have a spillover effect into zones where maybe you wouldn't think that psychological safety has anything to do with a person's sentiment about the workplace.
sentences.zh: 但它似乎还有一种溢出效应，延伸到那些你可能认为与心理安全感无关的领域，比如一个人对职场的感受。

sentences.en: To give you a concrete example, people who were reporting a culture of higher psychological safety at their workplace were also more satisfied with their salary.
sentences.zh: 举个具体的例子，那些报告称职场心理安全感文化较高的人，对薪水的满意度也更高。

sentences.en: Now, from this data, we can't say that one causes the other,
sentences.zh: 当然，从这些数据中，我们不能断定两者之间存在因果关系，

sentences.en: but we know that they're both co-occurring at a rate that's not just a coincidence and sort of it screams out for additional research on exactly that point.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道它们同时出现的频率并非巧合，这呼吁我们针对这一点进行更多的研究。

sentences.en: And what a wonderful thing that is, that people who feel safe at work are happier with almost every aspect of their work, even the income that they earn from it.
sentences.zh: 这真是一件美妙的事情，感到职场安全的人对工作的几乎每一个方面都更满意，甚至包括他们从中获得的收入。

sentences.en: What about for those employees who are struggling with burnout or a toxic workplace?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于那些正在经历职业倦怠或身处有毒职场的员工呢？

sentences.en: Are there any things that they can do to cope on an individual level?
sentences.zh: 他们在个人层面有什么应对方法吗？

sentences.en: How can employers help with that?
sentences.zh: 雇主又该如何提供帮助？

sentences.en: I would focus first on what can an employee, him or herself, do.
sentences.zh: 我会首先关注员工个人能做什么。

sentences.en: And as a first step, I'd suggest that they need to talk to somebody who they can truSt.
sentences.zh: 第一步，我建议他们需要找一个可以信任的人倾诉。

sentences.en: It could be really difficult to work through these kinds of issues by yourself in isolation.
sentences.zh: 独自一人去处理这些问题可能会非常困难。

sentences.en: So, talking to somebody who they trust, maybe it's a family member, maybe it's a friend, maybe it's a therapist,
sentences.zh: 所以，找一个信任的人谈谈，也许是家人、朋友或治疗师，

sentences.en: that can just really help a person process the situation and begin to sort out reality from misperception.
sentences.zh: 这真的能帮助一个人理清现状，开始区分现实与误解。

sentences.en: And if those conversations are beginning to reinforce a person's feeling that, wow,
sentences.zh: 如果这些对话开始强化一个人的感觉，即“哇，

sentences.en: this work situation that I'm in is actually toxic or it is adversely affecting my emotional and mental well-being, then it might be time to start considering their options.
sentences.zh: 我所处的这个工作环境确实是有毒的，或者它正在对我的身心健康产生负面影响”，那么也许是时候考虑其他选择了。

sentences.en: And that can mean a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着很多事情。

sentences.en: It can mean evaluating your own habits or your own habits contributing to this.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着评估你自己的习惯，或者你自己的习惯是否导致了这种情况。

sentences.en: And what I mean by that is there are folks, and I think we're all guilty of this from time to time,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些人——我想我们偶尔都会犯这种错——

sentences.en: who fall into the trap of obsessively checking our email and our messages and so on, even when it's not necessary.
sentences.zh: 陷入了强迫性查看电子邮件和消息的陷阱，即使在没必要的时候也是如此。

sentences.en: And we know it's not necessary.
sentences.zh: 而且我们知道这没必要。

sentences.en: And if we can break that habit, it could be one small step toward getting out of this burnout trap.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能改掉这个习惯，这可能是摆脱倦怠陷阱的一小步。

sentences.en: But, you know, in some instances, that may not be enough.
sentences.zh: 但是，在某些情况下，这可能还不够。

sentences.en: It might be looking beyond their own habits and looking at the workplace itself and asking themselves, is there some way that they can get relief in their current workplace?
sentences.zh: 这可能需要超越个人习惯，审视职场本身，问问自己：在当前的工作场所，有没有办法获得解脱？

sentences.en: Is there some way that by talking to their manager, talking to their HR department, raising these issues, they will get some relief, get some looking at their workload,
sentences.zh: 有没有办法通过与经理、人力资源部门沟通，提出这些问题，从而获得一些缓解，重新审视工作量，

sentences.en: figuring out how they can be happier in the workplace?
sentences.zh: 找出如何在职场中过得更开心的方法？

sentences.en: And in some workplaces, even that may not be possible.
sentences.zh: 在某些职场中，即使这样做也可能行不通。

sentences.en: And it just might be time to think about exploring other employment options.
sentences.zh: 那么是时候考虑探索其他就业选择了。

sentences.en: And certainly, I'm not encouraging people to make rash decisions or put themselves in an untenable economic situation.
sentences.zh: 当然，我不是在鼓励人们做出草率的决定或让自己陷入无法维持的经济困境。

sentences.en: But it's also untenable to just continue to work year after year in a situation that is harming your own health.
sentences.zh: 但年复一年地在损害自身健康的环境中工作也是不可持续的。

sentences.en: Are there lessons that employers can take from the survey?
sentences.zh: 雇主能从这项调查中吸取什么教训吗？

sentences.en: So, the number one lesson, when you look at the totality of the results,
sentences.zh: 当你审视所有结果时，最重要的教训是，

sentences.en: is that just so many things in the workplace seem to function much more smoothly when you create an atmosphere and a culture where everyone feels safe to express themselves and to contribute their thoughts and their ideas without any fear.
sentences.zh: 当你创造一种每个人都感到安全、可以毫无畏惧地表达自己并贡献想法和见解的氛围和文化时，职场中的许多事情似乎都能运行得更加顺畅。

sentences.en: We don't want people to be afraid at work.
sentences.zh: 我们不希望人们在工作中感到恐惧。

sentences.en: And so, fostering that sense of psychological safety is just absolutely key.
sentences.zh: 因此，培养这种心理安全感绝对是关键。

sentences.en: And if there's an employer out there who's listening to this podcast who is not familiar with the concept of psychological safety at work,
sentences.zh: 如果正在收听这个播客的雇主还不熟悉职场心理安全感的概念，

sentences.en: I really encourage them to get familiar with it.
sentences.zh: 我真的鼓励他们去了解一下。

sentences.en: There are tons of resources available to help employers learn about what it is and to learn tips for fostering it in their own organization.
sentences.zh: 有大量的资源可以帮助雇主了解它是什么，并学习在自己的组织中培养它的技巧。

sentences.en: It's as simple as a Google search to get started on this journey of learning about psychological safety.
sentences.zh: 只需在谷歌上搜索一下，就能开启这段学习心理安全感的旅程。

sentences.en: Now, I have seen personally absolutely no evidence that it does any harm, at least not when it's implemented correctly.
sentences.zh: 我个人从未见过任何证据表明它有任何害处，至少在正确实施的情况下是这样。

sentences.en: And I see lots and lots of evidence that it improves so many aspects of the workplace experience, which ultimately means it's good for the bottom line.
sentences.zh: 我看到了大量证据表明它改善了职场体验的许多方面，这最终意味着它对利润有好处。

sentences.en: And it means it's good for humanity.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着它对人类有益。

sentences.en: It's good for the workers.
sentences.zh: 这对员工有好处。

sentences.en: And that's not just at work, but what happens at work spills over into the rest of our lives.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是在工作中，工作中的经历也会溢出到我们生活的其他方面。

sentences.en: It affects us when we're driving home.
sentences.zh: 它会影响我们开车回家的心情。

sentences.en: It affects us once we walk in the door and we interact with our families and with our friends and so on.
sentences.zh: 它会影响我们走进家门后与家人、朋友互动的方式等等。

sentences.en: And if we can make everybody just, you know, 10%, 5%, 15% more psychologically safe at work, that's going to spill over and make us all a little bit better in our everyday lives.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能让每个人在工作中多出10%、5%或15%的心理安全感，那就会产生溢出效应，让我们的日常生活都变得更好一点。

sentences.en: Now, this is a survey that APA is doing every year.
sentences.zh: 这是美国心理学会（APA）每年都会进行的调查。

sentences.en: Have you started thinking about next year?
sentences.zh: 你们开始考虑明年的计划了吗？

sentences.en: What are some of the areas that you think you might want to be probing?
sentences.zh: 你认为你们可能想要深入探讨哪些领域？

sentences.en: That is a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: I think that there are a number of things that we want to drill down on a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们还有很多事情需要进一步深挖。

sentences.en: I think that the data with regard to physical and non-physical disabilities is striking and troubling.
sentences.zh: 我认为关于身体和非身体残障的数据是惊人且令人不安的。

sentences.en: And we need to drill down, not just to learn more about what the problems are, but to begin to try to figure out what are some possible solutions.
sentences.zh: 我们需要深入研究，不仅是为了了解问题所在，还要开始尝试找出可能的解决方案。

sentences.en: And how can we really begin to embrace people who are living with a disability in the workplace so that they're achieving the same level of psychological safety that other folks are?
sentences.zh: 我们如何才能真正开始接纳职场中的残障人士，让他们获得与其他员工同等水平的心理安全感？

sentences.en: I think that we also need to start taking a hard look in the survey about some of the relationships that employees have beyond just their manager relationship,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们还需要在调查中认真审视员工除了与经理关系之外的其他关系，

sentences.en: but the relationships that they have with employees in other departments, relationships that they have with HR.
sentences.zh: 比如他们与其他部门员工的关系，以及他们与人力资源部门的关系。

sentences.en: What are the levels of trust that they have with an HR department, with an accounting department, different aspects that are typically found in an average workplace?
sentences.zh: 他们对人力资源部门、会计部门以及典型职场中常见的各个部门的信任程度如何？

sentences.en: I think that it would just really be interesting to delve into.
sentences.zh: 我认为深入研究这些会非常有趣。

sentences.en: We're trying to get at what is the experience of working in America?
sentences.zh: 我们试图了解在美国工作的体验究竟是什么样的。

sentences.en: What is the experience of working in America vis-a-vis all of the other co-workers who you tend to interact with throughout the course of your day, your week,
sentences.zh: 在美国工作的体验，与你在一天、一周、

sentences.en: your year in the workplace?
sentences.zh: 一年中在职场中互动的其他同事相比，是怎样的？

sentences.en: Well, Dennis, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，丹尼斯，感谢你今天加入我的节目。

sentences.en: This has been very interesting, and I'm sure it's going to help our listeners, most of whom I think have to work.
sentences.zh: 这非常有意思，我相信这会对我们的听众有所帮助，我想他们大多数人都必须工作。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I've enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 我很享受这次交流。

sentences.en: If you want to read the full survey and the results, you can find that information on our website at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你想阅读完整的调查报告和结果，可以在我们的网站 APA.org 上找到相关信息。

sentences.en: Just search for Work in America.
sentences.zh: 只需搜索“Work in America”。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at SpeakingofPsychology.org or on Apple, Spotify, YouTube, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 SpeakingofPsychology.org 上，或者在 Apple、Spotify、YouTube 或任何你获取播客的地方找到《心理学谈话》往期的节目。

sentences.en: And if you like what you've heard, please leave us a review.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢你所听到的内容，请给我们留下评论。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at SpeakingofPsychology at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以发送电子邮件至 SpeakingofPsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由李·韦纳曼制作。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 代表美国心理学会，我是金·米尔斯。
